title: Paredes Sent Off for Grabbing García's Throat as Brawl Mars World Cup Final
excerpt: The Argentina midfielder was shown a red card after the final whistle for attacking two Spanish players, sparking a mass brawl that overshadowed Spain's second World Cup triumph.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Leandro Paredes received a red card for attacking Spain's Eric García after the World Cup final.
  • A mass brawl ensued at MetLife Stadium, involving players and staff from both teams.
  • FIFA is likely to impose a suspension on Paredes beyond the standard one-match ban.
  • Enzo Fernández was also sent off earlier in the match for a reckless challenge.
  • Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes was shown a straight red card after the final whistle for striking Spain's Eric García in the throat and shoving Gavi to the ground.
  • The incident sparked a mass brawl at MetLife Stadium, with players and staff from both sides involved in the altercation after Spain's 1-0 extra-time victory.
  • FIFA's disciplinary committee is expected to investigate, with Paredes likely facing a suspension beyond the standard one-match ban for a red card.
  • Paredes was the second Argentina player sent off, after Enzo Fernández received a second yellow card in the 93rd minute for a reckless challenge on Pau Cubarsí.

Paredes Charges at García After Final Whistle

Seconds after referee Slavko Vinčić blew the final whistle on Spain's 1-0 extra-time victory in the 2026 World Cup final, Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes charged across the pitch at MetLife Stadium and struck Spain defender Eric García with an open hand to the throat, knocking him to the ground.

The attack happened directly in front of assistant referee Tomaž Klančnik and within view of Argentina head coach Lionel Scaloni. Paredes then shoved Spain midfielder Gavi to the turf, triggering a mass confrontation that drew players and coaching staff from both sides onto the field. Argentina's Nahuel Molina also appeared to throw a punch at a Spanish substitute who had rushed on to celebrate.

> **"La Roja controlled the final from start to finish, registering 31 touches in the opposition box to Argentina's eight, while Argentina managed just two shots on target across 120 minutes."**

"Spain won their second World Cup title, adding to their 2010 triumph in South Africa.</p> <blockquote class="pull-quote"><p>"We wanted to go all out for this final."

Vinčić showed Paredes a straight red card once the brawl was brought under control, making him the second Argentina player to be dismissed. Enzo Fernández had earlier been sent off for a second yellow card in the 93rd minute after a wild challenge on Spain's teenage defender Pau Cubarsí.

"Paredes threw two or three haymakers into someone's face. He went for them. There is no place or space for that. We know how much it means to them and we know how much it hurts to lose, but there is a way to lose."

— Alan Shearer, BBC analyst

FIFA Disciplinary Action Expected

FIFA's disciplinary committee is almost certain to review the incident and could hand Paredes a lengthy ban. A straight red card carries an automatic one-match suspension, but violent conduct after the final whistle — particularly in a World Cup final — typically draws stiffer punishment under FIFA regulations. The 32-year-old Roma midfielder could face a multi-match ban that would carry into future international fixtures.

Brawl Erupts After Final Whistle

The scenes drew fierce criticism from pundits and fans. British broadcaster Piers Morgan called Argentina "just a bunch of nasty violent thugs, and a disgrace to football," adding he had "never been so happy to see a team lose." The backlash was amplified by Argentina's behaviour throughout the tournament — Valentín Barco and Cristian Romero had celebrated goals in the faces of England players during the semi-final, and the squad displayed a banner referencing the Falklands after that victory.

A Dominant Spain Denied a Clean Celebration

The brawl overshadowed what had been a commanding performance by Spain. La Roja controlled the final from start to finish, registering 31 touches in the opposition box to Argentina's eight, while Argentina managed just two shots on target across 120 minutes. Lionel Messi finished the match without recording a single shot — a footnote in what may have been his final game in the national team shirt.

Ferran Torres scored the only goal in the 106th minute, smashing home from close range after Nico Williams nodded a Pedro Porro cross back across goal. Spain won their second World Cup title, adding to their 2010 triumph in South Africa.

"We wanted to go all out for this final. To win it. The first idea was to keep Messi at bay, but also other players. Today we were convinced that this was our final."

— Luis de la Fuente, Spain head coach

A Pattern of Post-Match Incidents

Argentina have developed a reputation for aggressive behaviour in defeat at major tournaments. Paredes himself was involved in a touchline confrontation during the 2022 World Cup quarter-final against the Netherlands, when he kicked the ball into the Dutch bench. The broader pattern — from the semi-final Falklands banner to the post-final brawl — will likely prompt FIFA to take a firm stance, particularly given the global audience watching the final at MetLife Stadium.
